title: Blocking a punt: how the punt team protects the kick (and how two tips swung Thanksgiving)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run. It still holds one game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, "Eagles at Bears, Week 3", no snaps logged) and no review files. It was last updated Oct 12. The original football-film-room repo can't be read from this scheduled run (GitHub said access to it "is not enabled for this session"). So there are no new misses of yours to target. This lesson takes two punt plays that decided Thursday's games, one of them the board's Eagles bet.

The big idea: a punt is a race against the clock.The snap travels about 14 yards back. The punter catches it, takes two steps and kicks. That takes about 2 seconds.If one rusher reaches the spot where the ball leaves the foot in time, he blocks it.The punt team's whole formation is built to stop that one free rusher.

Letters match the list below. White = punt team. Yellow = the rush.

  1. A · Long snapper. The center on punts. He snaps the ball about 14 yards, then blocks.
  2. B · Wings. They stand a yard behind the tackles, one on each side.Their job is the edge. The fastest rushers come from outside, where the path to the punter is shortest.
  3. C · Personal protector. About 5 yards deep. He's the punt team's quarterback.He counts the rushers, calls the protection, and blocks anyone who comes free up the middle.
  4. D · Punter. About 14 yards deep. Closer is faster, but easier to block.
  5. E · The block point. About a yard in front of the punter, where the ball leaves his foot.Rushers aim there, not at the punter. Hitting the punter is roughing the kicker: 15 yards and a first down.
  6. F · Gunners. The two wide men don't block. They sprint downfield to tackle the returner.So the punt team protects with 8 players. The defense can send more to one side.

How a block happens: the defense overloads one side, like the two extra rushers on the right of the diagram.If that side has more rushers than blockers, one runs free to E. It's the same counting you do for the box (Lesson 19).

Thursday, Dallas: the Eagles' Ty Robinson blocked a Cowboys punt. Kenny Moore picked it up and scored.That was 7 of the Eagles' 39 points. The board's "Eagles over 19.5" → NO lost, and special teams were part of why.Thursday, Buffalo: with seconds left, the Bills' Joe Andreessen got a hand on Matt Araiza's punt.The tipped punt came up short. Greg Dortch returned it 17 yards to the Chiefs' 39. Tyler Bass then won it from 57.

Why it matters for bets: blocked punts are rare, fewer than 1 in 100 NFL punts.But one swings field position by 30–40 yards, or scores outright. That's the "return TD" risk on every Under card, like today's Broncos-Steelers Under.

In the drill: on 4th down, look at the personal protector. A fake punt often goes to him with a direct snap.Then count each side: blockers vs. rushers. An extra rusher on one side means a block try is coming.

Check yourself: the defense puts four rushers outside the right tackle. Only the tackle and the wing are there to block. Who has to slide over? (The personal protector. He picks up the free rusher.)

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 6: Situations)

o: A spot about a yard in front of the punter
quiz.w: They aim at the block point, where the ball leaves the foot. Hitting the punter is roughing the kicker: 15 yards and a first down.

quiz.q: What is the personal protector's job?
o: Run downfield to tackle the returner
Count the rushers, call the protection and block a free rusher
Hold the ball for the kicker
quiz.w: He lines up about 5 yards deep and acts as the punt team's quarterback.

quiz.q: Why don't the gunners block on a punt?
o: They sprint downfield to tackle the returner
quiz.w: Gunners cover the kick. That leaves 8 players to protect, so the defense can overload one side.

quiz.q: What set up the Bills' 57-yard winning field goal Thursday?
o: A tipped Chiefs punt and a 17-yard return
quiz.w: Joe Andreessen got a hand on Matt Araiza's punt. Greg Dortch returned the short kick to the Chiefs' 39.
